html:
Western Australia was a British colony covering the western third of Australia, founded in 1829 as the Swan River Colony with its capital at Perth. The map shows it in 1880 and 1900, before it joined the Commonwealth of Australia in 1901.

For decades it grew slowly. Land was poor near the coast and labour was short, so from 1850 to 1868 the colony asked Britain to send convicts, after the eastern colonies had stopped taking them. Its last convict ship, in 1868, was the end of convict transportation to Australia. It was the last colony to win self-government, in 1890.

Then gold changed everything. Finds at Coolgardie in 1892 and Kalgoorlie in 1893 brought a rush of miners, many from the depressed eastern colonies, and the population more than tripled in the 1890s. Water had to be carried hundreds of kilometres to the goldfields by a pipeline finished in 1903. Western Australia joined Federation late, after a vote in 1900.

Its northern and inland country remained Aboriginal land in practice well into the 20th century, while pearling at Broome and cattle stations in the north used Aboriginal labour, often unpaid.
